BookMetadataUpdate.description:
PATCH /books/{book_id} body — a hand-typed correction, the free-
text counterpart to /books/{id}/enrichment/apply's pick-a-provider-
candidate flow (see enrichment.py). Every field optional and only
applied when actually present in the request body (see the route's
`exclude_unset=True`), so leaving a field out of the PATCH — not just
sending it null — is what means "don't touch this one". Deliberately
excludes story_arcs/story_arc_numbers: those drive smart-collection
membership (see kodex/collections/rules.py) and are meant to come from
ComicInfo.xml/an enrichment provider, not a free-text edit here.

edition_type (C) is the one field here that isn't actually a
BookMetadata column — it lives on Book itself (see Book.edition_type's
docstring) — but it's still the natural "hand-typed correction" this
endpoint is for, so it rides along in the same payload rather than
needing a separate PATCH just for one field; the route pulls it out
before applying the rest to `meta`.
BookMetadataUpdate.title: BookMetadataUpdate

DownloadClientType.description:
Which backend actually fetches a Download — see kodex/acquire/clients/
manager.py's dispatch. Named *Type to avoid colliding with
kodex/acquire/clients/base.py's DownloadClient ABC (the actual client
implementations this enum picks between). DIRECT_HTTP covers Anna's
Archive/GetComics (a plain file URL, no torrent/nzb protocol
involved) — streamed straight into the target library by the worker
itself, no external download client at all.
DownloadClientType.title: DownloadClientType

DownloadCreateIn.description:

C13) are created by their own dedicated search-result endpoints
instead, since those already have the file in hand rather than a
torrent/nzb link to hand off to a client.
DownloadCreateIn.title: DownloadCreateIn

DownloadFromAnnasArchiveIn.description:

DownloadFromAnnasArchiveIn.title: DownloadFromAnnasArchiveIn

DownloadFromGetComicsIn.description:

For a user whose phone is gone: turns two-step login off and removes
their passkeys, and logs them out everywhere.

A one-time link (three days) with which the user sets a password;
hand it over yourself. A new link replaces the last one.

get.description:
The current cached batch — see recommendations.py's docstring for
why generating a fresh one is a separate, explicit action rather than
happening automatically on every page load (cost + latency).

post.description:
The logged-in user lets an app on a device in: a one-time code for
the app, bound to its challenge.
Revokes the key the app called with.
The key for an approved app, in exchange for its code and verifier.

A password login. With two-step login on, the answer is a ticket for
POST /auth/login/second-step (or a passkey) instead of the account.

Finishes a password login with the authenticator app's code or a
recovery code.

Where to send the browser to link this account to the provider's:

Options for navigator.credentials.get: a login with any passkey for

otherwise) or a new one.

second step, when the account has one).

POST /auth/totp/confirm gets a code from it.

get.description:
Progress is LEFT JOINed for the *current* user only (see
reading_progress.py — this app has one shared catalog but per-user
progress), which also lets `read_status` filter on it directly in SQL
rather than in Python — unlike list_series's small, always-fetch-all
result set, a single series or root-level library listing can
genuinely be large enough (hundreds of issues) for `limit`/`offset` to
matter, so filtering has to happen before pagination, in the database.

`root_only` filters to series_id IS NULL (a mixed library's books with
no series) — needed as a real filter, not a client-side post-filter,
now that this endpoint paginates: a library/[id] page slicing "just
the root books" out of a paginated, mixed-series page would silently
lose books whenever a page happened to contain none.

Books whose file a scan couldn't find: hidden ones (missing_since
set) and ones an admin chose to keep showing anyway. Newest first.
Declared before /{book_id} so "missing" isn't parsed as an id.

patch.description:
Hand-typed metadata correction — MetadataEditDialog.tsx's save
action, the free-text counterpart to /enrichment/apply's pick-a-
candidate flow. Only fields actually present in the request body are
touched (exclude_unset, not "is it null") and the row is marked
MANUAL same as a confirmed provider match — see
app/enrichment/engine.py's _apply_result docstring: "A row already
matched by the user (source=MANUAL) never reaches this function in
the first place", i.e. this is the exact same protection, not a
parallel mechanism.

get.description:
Serves the book's cover. With a size, one of the generated WebP
sizes; without one, the downloaded original if there is one, else the
book's own first page for page-based formats, so the UI always has
something to show.

parameters.description: 200, 400 or 1000 px on the long edge, as WebP
parameters.name: size

schema.description: 200, 400 or 1000 px on the long edge, as WebP
schema.title: Size

post.description:
(Re-)run Guided View panel detection for a single book. Defaults to
force=True, same reasoning as /enrich above — a single-book trigger is
normally a deliberate re-do. Returns 202 even if guided_view_enabled is
off; the job itself is a fast no-op in that case (see
app/panels/service.py) rather than something worth rejecting here.

get.description:
The file's SHA-256 and size, for an app verifying a download (and
resuming one with Range on /file). Taken on the first ask, then kept
until the file changes.

post.description:
Re-run automatic enrichment for a single book. Defaults to
force=True (unlike the library-wide job) since a single-book trigger
is normally someone deliberately asking to redo it — pass force=false
to only fill in what's still blank instead. Has no effect on a book
whose metadata is marked MANUAL; use /enrichment/apply to change those.

Apply a manually chosen candidate (a volume from /search, or —
when payload.is_issue is set — a specific issue from
/volumes/{volume_id}/issues above) to this book. Overwrites existing
metadata fields with the provider's data (or, with B8's `fields` set,
just the chosen subset) and marks the row as MANUAL, so future
automatic re-enrichment runs leave it alone — the same protection a
hand-typed edit would get.

get.description:
B8 — a side-effect-free look at what /apply would change, field by
field, before committing to it (or to which fields to keep vs
replace). Same provider/is_issue validation as /apply; a 404 here
means the same as /apply returning changed=False for this candidate.

Search one provider for candidates to manually match against — used
when automatic enrichment couldn't find (or got wrong) a match. Defaults
to the provider the book's library type would normally use, and to the
book's series title (or its own title) as the search query.

parameters.description: Defaults to the book's series/title if omitted
parameters.name: query

schema.description: Defaults to the book's series/title if omitted
schema.title: Query

get.description:
The second step of manual matching (F): once a volume has been
picked from /search above, list its issues so the user can click the
exact one instead of relying on automatic number-matching (which
fails outright for a book whose issue number couldn't be parsed, and
can't tell an issue apart from a same-numbered collected edition —
see Book.edition_type). Comic Vine only, like list_issues_for_volume.

Serves the raw file — used directly by EPUB/PDF readers (epub.js and
pdf.js both fetch the whole file) and by Send-to-Device. CBZ/CBR paging
for the image reader instead goes through /pages/{n}.

post.description:
Undoes "Visa igen" for a book whose file is still missing — hides it
again right away instead of waiting for the next scan. Only allowed
for books an admin restored by hand (keep_visible_when_missing): any
other book's visibility is the scanner's call, based on whether its
file is actually there.

get.description:
The user's reading journal for this book, newest first: every
position each device reported (kodex.reading.journal).

[width, height] per page for the image reader (see
app/scanning/dimensions.py). `dimensions` is null while unknown: a CBR
is sized by a background job the first time this is asked for
(`pending` true), so the reader just works without sizes that once.
Declared before /pages/{page_index} so "dimensions" isn't parsed as
a page number.

One page of a CBZ/CBR/CB7/image-folder book: as stored, or as WebP
when it is narrowed, trimmed or in a format browsers can't show
(kodex.reading.pages).

parameters.description: Re-encode to WebP at most this wide
parameters.name: max_width

schema.description: Re-encode to WebP at most this wide
schema.title: Max Width

delete.description:
Withdraws a flag — the flagging reader themselves, or any admin,
can do this (same "own it or be an admin" scoping as removing a book
from a manual collection isn't — this is closer to withdrawing your
own request). A flag someone else already resolved (see /resolve) is
left alone; use /resolve to change a verdict instead.

post.description:
B6 (Page Manager) — any logged-in reader can flag a page (scanner
junk, a duplicate, corrupt). Idempotent: re-flagging a page that
already has an unresolved flag just returns the existing one (updating
reason/note) rather than erroring — a reader clicking the flag button
twice, or two readers flagging the same bad page, shouldn't 409.
A page with a *resolved* flag can be flagged again (e.g. an admin
"kept" it, but wants to revisit later — see the unique constraint,
which the DELETE endpoint below clears at resolve time... actually see
that route: resolving does not delete the row, so re-flagging instead
reopens it).

get.description:
Guided View panel boxes for one page — normalized (0..1) x/y/w/h in
reading order, see app/models/panel.py. Always an empty list (never a
404) when there's nothing to guide through: no detection has run yet,
detection found this page "not panel-able" (see app/panels/detector.py),
or settings.guided_view_enabled is off — the frontend's fallback is
identical in all three cases (show the full page), so it doesn't need
to tell them apart.

post.description:
Admin verdict on a flagged page — DELETED hides it from every
reader from now on (see Book.deleted_page_indices, computed in
_book_out_detail below); KEPT just closes the flag out with no
reader-facing effect. Never touches the source archive file — see
BookPageFlag's own docstring.

get.description:
Current reading position for this book, if any — used by the reader
frontend to resume where the user left off when opening a book. Returns
null rather than 404 when there's no progress yet: a book nobody has
started reading is a normal state, not an error.

put.description:
Called by the reader frontend on a debounce (every 5-10s or on page
change / unload). Saving progress un-dismisses the book, so resuming a
previously "removed" book naturally brings it back to the shelf.

Also the trigger for "Följda serier" (see Series.is_following and the
architecture plan's "Modul: Följda serier"): the first time ANY
progress is saved on a book that belongs to a series, that whole
series starts being checked weekly for new releases. Runs on every
save rather than just the first, but the `is_following` guard makes
every save after the first a no-op check, not a repeat write.

post.description:
Removes the book from the "Fortsätter läsa" shelf without resetting
the saved position.

"Visa igen": shows a book hidden because its file is missing, and
keeps showing it on later scans until the file turns up again (then it
goes back to hiding normally if it ever disappears). A no-op for a
book that isn't hidden.

Enqueues a Send-to-Device job for the current user's own Kindle
address (see kodex/delivery/kindle.py). 400s immediately, before
touching the queue, if there's nothing to send to — a missing address
is something the user fixes in their own settings, not worth a round
trip through the worker to discover.

Links one CBL reading list to a (new or existing, same idempotent
match-by-name-and-rule check as _ensure_arc_collections uses)
Collection, then immediately enqueues the first roster fetch so the
collection is useful right away instead of showing an empty roster
until someone happens to click refresh.

get.description:
Powers the card-grid Collections page (2026-09-11, modeled after
metron.cloud/reading-lists/) — each card needs a cover + book count,
computed here rather than left to the frontend so a smart collection
(no book rows of its own) works the same as a manual one. One query
per smart collection, for this user — see _resolve_book_ids.

post.description:
AI-generated collection (see app/ai/collections.py) — an admin
types a free-text theme, the configured LLM picks matching titles out
of the ALREADY-OWNED library (never something to acquire — that's
app/ai/recommendations.py's "För dig" feed instead, see
api/routes/ai.py), and this creates a normal manual Collection from
the result. Admin-only, same as every other collection-management
endpoint on this router.

A reading list (.cbl) as a manual collection of the listed books
that are here, in the list's order; the rest come back as missing.

Second step — creates a normal manual Collection from exactly the
book_ids the caller accepted out of the preview (see
preview_csv_import above), same shape as any other manual collection.

C14 — first step of importing a League of Comic Geeks or Goodreads
export (see kodex/collections/csv_import.py): parses + fuzzy-matches every
row against the local library, but creates nothing yet. Nothing
questionable lands in a collection automatically — the caller reviews
`needs_review`/`unmatched` and picks which book_ids to actually keep
before calling /import-csv/confirm.

C15 — an admin types (or pastes) a bare Comic Vine story-arc id to
start tracking a whole crossover/event from scratch, before owning a
single issue from it. Distinct from engine.py's _ensure_arc_collections,
which only ever auto-creates an arc's smart Collection reactively, the
first time an already-owned book happens to match it — this is the
same shape built proactively instead, then reuses the exact on-demand
roster-fetch job (refresh_story_arc_task) the "Uppdatera
platshållare"-button above already triggers. No separate placeholder
table/logic needed for the official reading order: StoryArcIssue rows
with book_id IS NULL already are the "Saknas" placeholders (Uppdrag 7
Del D).

delete.description:
Bulk counterpart to remove_book_from_collection below — symmetric
with add_books_to_collection's bulk-add shape, for a multi-select
"Ta bort ur samlingen" action (see BulkActionBar.tsx).

get.description:
The books in order: a manual collection's own, or what a smart
collection's rule matches for this user (kodex.collections.members).
The collection as a reading list (.cbl), in its order.

delete.description: Reverts a collection to its auto-computed cover.

post.description:
Manual cover for a collection (D) — takes priority over the
auto-computed "first book's cover" (see list_collections). Stored the
same way BookMetadata.cover_path already is (relative path under
settings.covers_dir), just in its own "collections" subfolder so a
collection id and a book id can never collide on the same filename.

put.description:
Sets an explicit reading order for a manual collection (E) —
`book_ids` in the exact order they should appear in from now on.
Only meaningful for manual collections: a smart collection's contents
(and order) are computed fresh from `rule` every time, there's no
per-book row to attach a position to. Must be the collection's full
current book set, not a subset — a partial list would silently leave
the missing books' old positions in place, mixed in with the new
ones in a way nobody asked for.

post.description:
"Begär saknade nummer" — the bulk counterpart to StoryArcPanel.tsx's
per-issue "Skapa önskemål" button, requested 2026-09-11 so requesting
an entire arc's gap (or whatever's left of it) doesn't mean clicking
through each placeholder one at a time. Creates one Request per
currently-missing StoryArcIssue, all tagged with this collection_id
(see Request.collection_id) so the admin queue can group/export them
together. Skips an issue that already has a non-rejected request with
the same title in this collection, so re-clicking after a partial
fetch (or just clicking twice) doesn't pile up duplicates.

Enqueues a fetch of this arc's full issue roster from Comic Vine —
see app/workers/tasks.py's refresh_story_arc_task and
app/enrichment/story_arc_roster.py for what that actually does (one
API call for the roster + batched calls for issue details). Admin-
only and on-demand rather than automatic: fetching a roster the first
time a book from that arc matches would mean doing it dozens of times
over for a big library-wide enrichment run before anyone's actually
asked to see the "what's missing" view for that specific arc.

Creates a NEEDS_REVIEW tracking row for a chosen Anna's Archive
result — deliberately does NOT enqueue start_download_task (there's
no download client to hand the link to): the admin visits
`detail_url`, fetches the file by hand, then places it via the B7
library-upload endpoint. This row just keeps the to-do visible in the
admin downloads list instead of getting lost in a browser tab.

Bridges a chosen GetComics result into a DIRECT_HTTP download —
unlike POST /downloads/from-search (qBittorrent/SABnzbd), there's no
separate download client to hand the link to, so this enqueues
fetch_direct_http_download_task instead of start_download_task.

Bridges a chosen Prowlarr search result into C10's existing
download pipeline — same Download row + start_download_task enqueue
as POST /downloads, just with the client derived from the result's
protocol instead of picked explicitly.

get.description:
Proxies a Prowlarr search — results aren't persisted here, only
returned for the admin to pick from via POST /downloads/from-search.

Proxies an Anna's Archive search — same non-persisted-results shape
as GET /downloads/search. See kodex/acquire/clients/annas_archive.py: this
source is interactive-only, so results only ever lead to POST
/downloads/from-annas-archive's manual-review tracking row, never an
automatic fetch.

Proxies a GetComics search via FlareSolverr — same non-persisted-
results shape as GET /downloads/search, for UI reuse. See
kodex/acquire/clients/scrapers/getcomics.py for the circuit breaker guarding
this against a FlareSolverr instance that's down.

delete.description:
Removes Kodex's own tracking row only — deliberately does NOT also
call the download client's own remove/cancel API (see kodex/acquire/clients/
qbittorrent.py/sabnzbd.py's remove()): this endpoint has never been
exercised against a real client in this deployment (see this module's
own docstring), and a destructive remote call is exactly the kind of
thing not to guess at working correctly. Cancelling in qBittorrent/
SABnzbd itself is a manual step for now.

post.description:
Called by the download client's own completion script (qBittorrent's
--run-on-torrent-finished / SABnzbd's completion script) — not an
authenticated Kodex user, so gated by a shared-secret query token
(settings.download_webhook_secret) instead of the normal OIDC session.
An empty secret means the feature isn't configured yet — refuses
every call rather than accepting an unauthenticated one by accident.

get.description:
Every job queued or running, and those that ended in the last day,
newest first. Polled by the admin job view (JobsPanel.tsx).

post.description:
Links one LoCG event to a (new or existing) Collection, then
immediately enqueues the first roster fetch — same idempotent
match-by-name-and-rule check and same reasoning as cbl.py's link().

Resolves a pasted URL to an event id + name, for the admin to
confirm before linking — mirrors picking a result in the CBL search,
just with one candidate instead of a list since there's nothing to
search against.

patch.description:
Rename a library and/or change its type. A type change only affects
future enrichment/merging decisions; existing metadata is left as is.

get.description:
The admin-upload file browser's data source (ReadMeABook-inspired —
see claude/omnibus-och-ai-forbattringar.md's "Övriga UX-idéer" note):
lists a folder's subfolders (with a recursive importable-file count
each, so an admin can tell "Absolute Corvid" already has 12 issues
without opening it) and loose importable files, so LibraryFileUpload
on the frontend can offer real navigation instead of a blind
free-text subfolder field. Read-only — never creates or touches
anything on disk, unlike POST .../upload below.

post.description:
Enqueue a Guided View panel-detection pass for every page-based book
in one library. Manual and per-library, same convention as /enrich and
/fulltext-index above — no automatic scheduling on scan. See
app.config.Settings.guided_view_enabled for the global kill switch;
this endpoint stays enabled either way (it's a fast no-op per book when
the flag is off) so there's nothing to remember to re-guard once it's
turned back on.

Enqueue an automatic metadata-enrichment pass for one library.

Only touches books with thin metadata unless force=True is passed, and
never touches a book whose metadata is already marked MANUAL (a
previous manual match, or a future hand-edit) — see
app/enrichment/engine.py. Books that still don't get a match after this
can be fixed individually via /books/{id}/enrichment/search + /apply.

Enqueue a full-text extraction + indexing pass for one library.

Manual and per-library on purpose (see the architecture plan): unlike
metadata indexing, this is never run automatically on scan, since
extracting the text of every EPUB chapter / PDF page in a library is
far more expensive than reading its metadata. CBZ/CBR books have no
text layer and are skipped. Sets Library.last_fulltext_indexed_at when
the job completes.

B9 — restores metadata from every series.json found under this
library's folder (see app/scanning/series_json.py) onto Book rows a
scan has already created. Run this after a rescan when recovering
from a lost/corrupted database — see that module's own docstring for
the full recovery story. Synchronous (not queued): this is JSON
parsing + plain DB upserts, not archive decoding, so even a library
with hundreds of series.json files finishes in well under RQ's
default job timeout.

Enqueue a scan job for one library. Fulltext indexing is a separate,
equally manual, per-library trigger — added in a later phase — kept
apart from scanning on purpose (see the architecture plan).

B7 — admin drops a single book file (CBZ/CBR/EPUB/PDF) straight
into a library folder from the browser, then triggers the same scan
job /scan already does — the manual-request-fulfillment counterpart to
the request queue (see requests.py): approve a request, then land the
file here instead of needing shell/file-manager access to the server.

Also the landing point for a headless folder-watcher script on an
external download-manager host (Mylar3/Kapowarr — see requests.py's
send_to_mylar3/send_to_kapowarr and app/config.py's upload_api_key
docstring): require_admin_or_upload_key accepts either a normal
admin session (browser) or a shared X-Kodex-Upload-Key header
(script), so this one endpoint serves both.

`subfolder` (optional) is a relative path inside the library, e.g. a
series folder name — resolved and checked to still be inside the
library root before anything is written, so neither it nor the
filename can escape via "..".

get.description:
Exact duplicates (the same pages; the first book in each group is the
one the others point at) and similar books (same number in the same
series, nearly the same cover, different pages).

post.description:
Accepts the best candidate of, or marks "no match" on, several open
reviews at once. Each can be undone with /revert (which reopens it).

Searches with another title (or one provider) and returns scored
candidates; nothing is applied.

get.description:
The "Fortsätter läsa" shelf: books with progress between 0 and 100%
that the user hasn't dismissed, newest first.

put.description: Which collection the device syncs; null syncs nothing.

post.description:
(Re-)generates the user's OPDS token. Any previous token stops
working immediately — there's only ever one active token per user.

Bulk counterpart to PUT /books/{id}/progress — "Markera som läst"/
"Markera som oläst" over a multi-select in a grid view (see
BulkActionBar.tsx). User-scoped like every other progress endpoint
here, not admin-only: marking your own books read/unread is a
personal action, same as reading a book normally would be.

get.description:
Books finished per month, the days something was read, streaks and
pages, over the last year.

`resolved=false` (the admin inbox's default view) shows the review
queue; omit the filter to see everything, including past verdicts.

post.description:
Queues copying these books to another server's library, each into the
series folder it has here. The outcome per book shows under Admin › Jobb.

get.description:
Per server: its libraries (to copy into) and whether it has each of
this series' books. A server that can't be reached comes back with
``error``; the others still answer.

Pull-list across every followed series — see release_check.py's
weekly sync for how SeriesReleaseEvent rows get here in the first
place. `status` filters client-relevant computed status; unfiltered
(the default) returns everything, sorted soonest/most-recent first
(nulls — a Comic Vine issue with no known store_date yet — last).

post.description:
Hides one event from the pull-list without pretending it's owned —
see SeriesReleaseEvent.dismissed's own docstring. Any logged-in user,
not admin-only: this is closer to a shared household preference (like
following a series itself) than a destructive/management action.

get.description:
The admin queue — every request across every user, optionally
filtered by status. Ordered oldest-first (unlike "mine" above, which is
newest-first) so a pending backlog gets worked in the order it came
in.

CSV export of the admin queue, respecting the same filters as the
on-screen list (status, and optionally scoped to one collection) —
"smidigt sätt att exportera ut" a batch of requests to hand off to
whoever actually sources comics, requested 2026-09-11 alongside the
"Begär saknade nummer" bulk action below. BOM-prefixed UTF-8 so Excel
renders å/ä/ö correctly, same convention narvaro's own CSV exports
use.

post.description:
Batch-C tie-in (C10-C11) — opt-in, never automatic on its own. An
admin explicitly calls this (e.g. from an "attempt automatic
download" checkbox when approving a request) to search Prowlarr for
the request's own title. A single safe-enough top match (see
_best_title_match) is queued immediately, exactly like a manual
POST /downloads/from-search pick would be, with request_id set so
import_completed_download_task marks this Request FULFILLED once it
lands. Anything less certain — no match, an unreachable Prowlarr, a
lot of similarly-scored candidates — leaves the request untouched
(still PENDING/APPROVED) for the existing manual search-and-place
flow to handle; auto_download_enabled is still recorded either way,
so the admin queue can show an attempt was made.
Same shape as send_to_mylar3 above — see its own docstring.

Requested 2026-09-21 alongside Kapowarr below — Mylar3 runs on a
separate, user-managed host and does its own search/download/organize
once told which Comic Vine volume to track; Kodex has no visibility
into when a file actually lands (unlike the qBittorrent/SABnzbd
Download-row pipeline above). The finished file arrives back into
Kodex later via that host's own script hitting POST /libraries/{id}/
upload (B7) — see app/config.py's upload_api_key docstring for how
that script authenticates. No Download row here: there's nothing for
Kodex to track. request.status is left alone (an admin marks it
FULFILLED by hand once the file shows up) — auto_download_enabled is
still recorded either way, matching the Prowlarr flow's own "the
admin queue can show an attempt was made" reasoning.

get.description: The snippet is escaped HTML with the hit in <mark></mark>.

`following=true` is the "Följer"-vy's data source (see
web/src/routes/_authed/_shell/following.tsx) — series with a new
release sort first there, so someone following a lot of series doesn't
have to hunt for the ones that actually changed.

read_count/in_progress_count are joined against the *current* user's
own ReadingProgress rows only — this app has one shared catalog but
per-user progress (see reading_progress.py), so two users browsing the
same library see the same books but different progress badges.
`read_status` filters on those computed counts in HAVING, and
`limit`/`offset` page in SQL, so a library with thousands of series
only builds (and finds covers for) the page asked for.

post.description:
Enqueue an on-demand run of the weekly followed-series release
check — the same job kodex.jobs.periodic enqueues every Monday
automatically once a week, exposed here so an admin doesn't have to
wait up to seven days to see it work (or re-check right after fixing
something, e.g. adding a missing COMICVINE_API_KEY). See
app/enrichment/release_check.py for what the check actually does.

get.description:
Backs the alphabet jump bar (A3) on library/series listing pages —
a cheap single-column query (just `sort_title`) rather than the full
`GET /series` response, since the jump bar only needs where each
letter starts, not every series' full payload. Mirrors list_series's
`library_id`/`following` filters and its empty-series exclusion
(`Series.books.any()`, an EXISTS — same rows list_series would show,
just without needing the book_count/read_count aggregation it does)
so the jump bar's counts always match what's actually on the page.

post.description:
B9 — writes/overwrites series.json in this series' own library
folder (see app/scanning/series_json.py). 400 when the series has no
books, or its books don't share one folder (see export_series).

Manual follow — previously the only way a series became followed was
implicitly, the first time reading_progress.py's save_progress saw
progress saved on one of its books (see Series.is_following/followed_at
there). This is the explicit counterpart for a series you want to
watch for new releases without having started reading it yet.

get.description:
B5 — this one series' known issues (Comic Vine only, see
release_check.py's _sync_release_events), soonest/most-recent
store_date first. See GET /releases for the aggregated pull-list
across every followed series.

schema.title: Response Series List Series Release Events

get.description: The user's connected trackers for a series: linked, or with the id the matcher found there.

post.description: Sends the series' progress to every linked tracker now.

put.description: Links the series to the service's entry and sends its progress at once.

post.description:
Stops future release checks/notifications for this series.
followed_at is deliberately left as-is (not cleared) — it records when
the series was *first* followed, which stays true/useful history even
after unfollowing; is_following is the only field that actually gates
app/enrichment/release_check.py's weekly check.

get.description:
What changed after ``since`` (start with 0), a page at a time: ask
again with ``cursor`` while ``more`` is true. ``reset`` means the
server's history doesn't go back to the cursor: start over from 0.
Positions come after ``progress_since`` with their own cursor.

delete.description: Forgets the account and the series linked with it; nothing changes at the service.

post.description: The service's login page for an OAuth service (AniList, MyAnimeList); it comes back to the callback.
Connects a password service (MangaUpdates, Kitsu). The password isn't kept; the service's token is.

Queues a scan: sent once by another server after copying a batch of
books here (each upload skips its own scan).

For each book, whether a visible book here is the same file
(content_hash) or the same volume (series title, number and edition
type: another release of it).

put.description: Always 200: kosync clients treat anything else as a sync failure.

get.description:
A page for PSE; ``width`` is the client's {maxWidth}, which some send
unfilled. Fetching a page is how a PSE client says where it is.
